prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words)

Economic strategy and investment
- Create a Sustainable Investment Board; factor climate impacts into fiscal forecasts.
- Establish a £400bn National Transformation Fund (including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund).
- Create a National Investment Bank and Regional Development Banks to lend £250bn over 10 years.
- Tighten green finance rules and delist companies that fail climate responsibilities.

Climate, energy and industry
- Aim for most emissions cuts by 2030; target ~90% renewable/low‑carbon electricity and 50% low‑carbon heat by 2030.
- Build large-scale wind and solar; support nuclear, tidal, hydrogen, storage and interconnectors.
- Retrofit almost all 27m homes to high efficiency; zero‑carbon standard for new homes; permanent fracking ban.
- Windfall tax on oil producers; support a just transition and protect energy workers.
- Public ownership of energy networks and water; regional energy agencies with fuel poverty and decarbonisation duties.
- At least 1m green jobs; expand R&D to 3% of GDP; sector plans for steel, recycling, gigafactories and supply chains.
- Producer responsibility for waste; deposit return schemes; action on plastic and recycling.

Transport and environment
- Public ownership of rail; network reintegration, electrification, HS2 to Scotland, Crossrail for the North.
- Empower councils to run/regulate buses; restore routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils take control.
- Accelerate zero‑emission vehicles and charging; expand cycling/walking.
- Clean Air Act; £5.6bn for flood defences; stronger protections for nature, trees, habitats and watchdogs.

Digital, culture, media, sport, gambling
- Free nationwide full‑fibre broadband by 2030 via a new public operator; digital rights and online duty of care.
- Arts Pupil Premium; £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; media plurality reforms; protect over‑75s’ TV licences.
- Football governance reforms (fan representation, safe standing, grassroots funding).
- New Gambling Act: ad curbs in sport, limits, levy and redress.

Public services, health and care
- Reverse outsourcing presumption; insource where viable; £150bn Social Transformation Fund for schools, hospitals, care homes and housing.
- Restore public‑sector pay with above‑inflation rises (5% first year).
- NHS: average 4.3% annual funding growth; end privatisation; upgrade diagnostics and IT; abolish prescription charges; free annual dental check‑ups; expand mental health and children’s services; recruit and train staff; net‑zero NHS.
- National Care Service: free personal care for older people; lifetime cap on care costs; improve workforce pay/conditions; increase Carer’s Allowance.

Education and skills
- Sure Start Plus; 30 hours free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds; extend paid maternity leave to 12 months; recruit ~150k early years staff.
- Schools: increased funding; max primary class size 30; scrap KS1/2 SATs; Arts Premium; replace Ofsted; local oversight of all schools; free primary school meals.
- Lifelong learning: free Level 3; six years at Levels 4–6 with maintenance grants; restore EMA and ESOL; strengthen FE.
- Higher education: abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; post‑qualification admissions; tackle casualisation.

Work, pay and rights
- Real Living Wage of at least £10 for all 16+; sectoral collective bargaining; day‑one rights; ban zero‑hours; single worker status; stronger union rights.
- Target 32‑hour average full‑time week within a decade (no loss of pay) via productivity and bargaining.
- Workers’ Protection Agency; tackle late payments; employee ownership funds up to 10% in large firms; explore UBI pilots.
- Family rights: extend maternity/paternity, flexible work, paid bereavement leave.

Housing and communities
- Build 1m+ council/social homes over a decade; at least 150k/year, including 100k council homes for social rent.
- Redefine “affordable” to local incomes; end Right to Buy; English Sovereign Land Trust; brownfield priority.
- Private renting: rent caps linked to inflation (with local powers), open‑ended tenancies, national licensing, renters’ unions; regulate short‑lets.
- End rough sleeping in five years; 8,000 additional homes; raise Local Housing Allowance to 30th percentile.
- £1bn fire safety fund; enforce cladding replacement; upgrade high‑rise safety.

Social security, disability, pensions
- Replace Universal Credit; immediate mitigations: advance payments, suspend sanctions, split/fortnightly payments, direct-to-landlord, scrap benefit cap/two‑child limit, scrap bedroom tax, raise LHA; replace DWP with a supportive Department for Social Security; child well‑being strategy.
- Disability: end outsourced assessments (bring in‑house); raise key disability benefits; expand Access to Work; increase Carer’s Allowance.
- Pensions: maintain triple lock; keep state pension age at 66; improve dashboards and commissions; address 1950s women’s losses; reform mineworkers’ scheme sharing; uprate overseas pensions.

Policing, justice, security
- Recruit additional police and rebuild neighbourhood policing; public health approach to drugs; minimum victim service standards.
- Justice: restore legal aid early advice; reunify probation; presumption against short non‑violent sentences; more prison officers; no new private prisons; stronger protections against VAWG.
- Cybersecurity overhaul; border controls review.

Constitution, democracy and funding
- Abolish House of Lords and replace with an elected Senate after a constitutional convention; decentralisation and regional offices.
- Repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; scrap voter ID plans.
- Tighten political funding and lobbying rules; extend FOI; restrict paid second jobs for MPs.

Migration and refugees
- End the “hostile environment”; scrap 2014 Act; end indefinite detention; close two detention centres; humane asylum with safe routes and right to work; protect family life.
- Grant EU nationals automatic rights (declaratory system); seek reciprocal EU protections.

Brexit
- Within six months: a public vote between a new “leave” deal (customs union, close single‑market alignment, rights and standards guarantees, security cooperation) and remain; implement result.

International
- War Powers Act; invest in diplomacy and climate leadership; suspend arms sales implicated in rights abuses; recognise Palestine; increase UN peacekeeping funds; maintain NATO and renew the nuclear deterrent; veteran support and MoD climate plan.

International development and trade
- Retain DfID and 0.7% aid; add inequality goal; strengthen public services and tax capacity; £4bn/year international climate finance; end fossil‑fuel export finance; reform CDC; food sovereignty fund.
- Human‑rights‑led trade, stricter export controls, transparency in trade deals; improve global access to medicines.
